t: This is Herbert House, a Grade II* listed building on Kennington Lane in Kennington, a former orphanage. It was designed by John Loughborough Pearson, a Gothic Revival architect best known for his churches and cathedrals. Pearson worked on at least two hundred and ten ecclesiastical buildings in England over a career of fifty-four years, and he was especially admired for his skill at vaulting. So this is a rarer thing to find from his hand, a building made to house children rather than to hold a congregation.
